title: Model Usage
text: raw ENMs retrieved using method can used regular e1071 SVM model objects. Alternatively, helper function elements::predict_occ_taxon retrieves model using method , generates predictions, formats results data frame. additional helper function elements::predict_occ can generate predictions multiple taxa, either specifing taxa model ‘taxa_codes’ argument, setting ‘taxa_codes’ NULL including additional column predictors data frame named ‘taxon_code’. Two helper arguments provide additional functionality controlling model use. First, ‘limit’ argument, assigns probability values zero one predictors outside specified range e.g. 10% 90% quantiles (see elements::NicheWidths). Second, ‘holdopt’ argument, holds specified variable values optima (defined mean value present elements::NicheWidths). simple demonstration, two sets predictions Stellaria graminea generated, holding variables apart N optima: 1) limit set, 2) limit set 1% 99% quantiles.  Please note ten eleven variables held optima predicted probabilities high influence unsuitable N values partially offset. Consequently, shape response curves wider corresponding PDP plot produced elements::plot_me function (see Model Inspection section ).
code: results <- elements::predict_occ_taxon(taxon = "stellaria_graminea", predictors = elements::ExampleData1, pa = "Present", limit = NULL, dp = 2, append_predictors = FALSE) #>   Present #> 1    0.30 #> 2    0.00 #> 3    0.00 #> 4    0.70 #> 5    0.01 #> 6    0.08 results <- elements::predict_occ(taxa_codes = NULL, predictors = elements::ExampleData2, pa = "Present", limit = NULL, dp = 2, append_predictors = FALSE) #>     Present         taxon_code #> 201    0.70 silene_flos-cuculi #> 202    0.00 silene_flos-cuculi #> 203    0.12 silene_flos-cuculi #> 204    0.00 silene_flos-cuculi #> 205    0.00 silene_flos-cuculi #> 206    0.00 silene_flos-cuculi n_gradient <- data.frame("N" = seq(0, 10, 0.01))  vary_N_no_limit <- elements::predict_occ_taxon(taxon = "stellaria_graminea", predictors = n_gradient,                                                pa = "Present", limit = NULL, holdopt = c("bio05", "bio06", "bio16", "bio17", "GP", "L", "M", "R", "S", "SD"),                                                dp = 2, append_predictors = TRUE)  vary_N_limit <- elements::predict_occ_taxon(taxon = "stellaria_graminea", predictors = n_gradient,                                             pa = "Present", limit = "q01_q99", holdopt = c("bio05", "bio06", "bio16", "bio17", "GP", "L", "M", "R", "S", "SD"),                                             dp = 2, append_predictors = TRUE)

title: Model Usage
text: elements designed used model scenarios environmental change considering multiple interacting drivers. object elements::ExampleScenarios provides basic set example scenarios: () Climate Change - RCP4.5, () Climate Change - RCP8.5, (B) Grazing Intensification (+0.025GP per year), (B) Grazing Reduction (-0.025GP per year), (C) Nutrient Enrichment (+0.25N per year) along Baseline scenario. predicted probabilities taxa elements::ExamplePlot Scenario C displayed.

title: Model Usage
text: elements can also used filter species pools based given set predictor values using function elements::env_filter. Two sets methods available: 1) “svm” generates predictions using elements::predict_occ uses resultant probability values; 2) “mean” “median” calculates normalised euclidean distance values supplied ‘predictors’ argument mean median niche positions present elements::NicheWidths. example, elements::env_filter applied taxa elements::TaxonomicBackbone using svm method, predictors derived baseline environmental variable data elements::ExamplePlot present elements::ExampleScenarios[1,]. NOTE: mean median methods included demonstrative purposes used practice consider joint distribution variables expressed SVM model hypervolumes.

title: Ecological niche models for the plants of Europe
text: elements R package containing correlative, realised Ecological Niche Models (ENMs) prevalent vascular plants, bryophytes, terricolous lichens European Vegetation Archive (EVA) (Chytrý et al., 2016). code used produce models available https://github.com/NERC-CEH/elementsAnalysis.

title: Ecological niche models for the plants of Europe
text: ENMs adhere Hutchinsonian conceptualisation ecological niche n-dimensional hypervolume (Hutchinson, 1957). environmental variables forming dimensions hypervolume consist : M - Soil Moisture1 R - Reaction1 N - Soil Nitrogen1 L - Light1 GP - Grazing Pressure2 SD - Soil Disturbance2 S - Salinity3 bio05 - Maximum temperature warmest month4 bio06 - Minimum temperature coldest month4 bio16 - Precipitation wettest quarter4 bio17 - Precipitation driest quarter4 Support Vector Machine (SVM) models, form hyperplane presence absence hypervolumes, trained tested using using mlr3 ecosystem R packages (Lang et al., 2019). raw e1071 (Meyer et al., 2024) SVM models bundled elements. information please see Marshall et al (prep). 1(Dengler et al., 2023), 2(Midolo et al., 2023), 3(Tichy et al., 2023), 4(Copernicus Climate Change Service, 2021)

title: elements 0.5.5 (18/09/2025)
text: Full model training re-run addressing outstanding taxonomic alignment issues. Now 6631 taxa. Bundling imbalance information elements::Imbalances Re-creating elements::TaxonomicBackbone object, now using GBIF EuroSL include lichen hybrid taxa. also align taxonomic backbone EIVE1.5 “Euro+Med augmented” taxonomy upon release EIVE1.5. Changing pkgdown site theme sandstone. Improving elements::startup, now creates new environment (elementsEnv) parent environment contains ENMs, rather simply loading ENMs directly global environment.

title: elements 0.5.4 (27/06/2025)
text: Adding pdf package manual. Moving README content articles. Adding pkgdown website.

title: elements 0.5.3 (20/06/2025)
text: Removing superfluous code elements::predict_occ. Including example code running scenario c README. Adding Zenodo README badge. Adding function elements::env_filter, filters given set taxa using set predictor variables retain suitable taxa .
